create.name: Geshe Dorji Damdul
create.bio:
Geshe Dorji Damdul is a Tibetan Buddhist monk and scholar who has directed Tibet House in New Delhi, the Dalai Lama's cultural centre in the Indian capital, since 2011. He trained in the Gelug monastic curriculum and in 2002 was awarded the Geshe Lharampa, the highest degree of that system, by Drepung Loseling Monastic University. Alongside his teaching he has edited and co-written books on Buddhist philosophy, theory of knowledge and science, and his long exchanges with physicists shape the way he presents classical ideas to modern students.

At Tibet House he is the main teacher of the Nalanda courses, structured programmes in classical Indian Buddhist philosophy that run from short certificate courses to a multi-year masters course. They are taught in English, in person in Delhi and online, with recordings, review sessions and group discussion, and fees are kept low so that anyone can join. His teaching moves from the basics of mind and karma to emptiness, dependent origination and the bodhisattva path, and he pairs study with contemplation and meditation. He also leads residential study retreats, such as a nine-day retreat on Shantideva's chapter on patience at Tushita Meditation Centre in Dharamkot in 2026, many of whose sessions are freely available on the Tibet House YouTube channel.

courses.title: Nalanda Certificate Course (Batch 4)
courses.description: A 22-week online course in the Nalanda tradition of Buddhist philosophy, taught in English with two teaching sessions and a review session each week and recordings for self-paced study. It includes guidance on meditation, and fees are subsidised, with lower rates for students and past participants.
